correctness.rationale: For fixed points d_i=||x_i-y_i|| <= (Ad)_i; w>0, w^T(Ad-d)=0 forces Ad=d and PF simplicity yields d=c u. The strictly convex triangle equality pins the image of every convex combination, making an affine scaled isometry graph when K convex. In the scalar case distances to two anchors uniquely set every coordinate on the same signed Perron line, even for nonconvex K. Row-stochastic normalization P_ij=a_ij*u_j/u_i and clipped averaging exhibit every signed compact interval; propagation of an attaining maximum in irreducible P proves absence of other fixed points. For residual q=(I-A)d <= e and w^Tq=0, weighted L1(q)<=2w^T e; Z invertible on Perron line/complement yields the claimed estimate. These are general arguments, not finite tests.
